prompt:

Behind her, a richly painted background with layered painterly colour, subtle visible brushwork, atmospheric perspective and cinematic depth. Luminous, rich colours; crisp focal details on the face and costume, softer painted edges toward the distance. No flat single-tone cel shading, photographic appearance, semi-realistic face or plastic 3D-render finish. Keep this rendering exactly as in the attached image — the same finish, line, shading, skin and colour treatment.

Place: an outdoor bath, stream or fountain built in the style of her element's kingdom
Weather / season: spring — blossom petals drifting outside.
Time of day: dawn — the first pale light, cool and quiet, the sky just turning; a pale lilac sky, mist low on the ground.
Hair: her hair let down loose over her shoulders — same colour and length as the attached image.
Light direction: backlit — the main light comes from behind her, a bright rim along her hair and shoulders.

COMPOSITION: a full-body shot, her complete head, hands and feet inside the frame with restrained margins; body turned three-quarters toward the camera; head turned to the side; camera slightly below, looking up at her.
Lens / perspective: 35mm-equivalent environmental perspective balancing the woman and the setting with moderate depth.
RIGHT HAND: her own right hand rests on her hip.
LEFT HAND: her own left hand rests naturally for the posture, relaxed and empty.
GAZE: she looks toward the far distance.
EXPRESSION: soft distant eyes, faint wistful half-smile, brows gently raised at the inner ends.

Leave behind everything she wears in the attached image — no crown, tiara, helmet, feathers, headpiece, hairpins from it, armour or regalia; her hair is styled for the everyday outfit, with at most one small accessory.

Her element — ytterbium: a soft, ductile, bright silvery metal named for the Swedish village of Ytterby, separated in 1878 in Geneva from erbia, with its younger sister lutetium still hidden inside it until 1907; held one by one in an egg-crate lattice of light, its atoms tick to a steady yellow laser more than five hundred trillion times a second in optical clocks so exact they would not lose a second over the age of the universe and can feel time run faster when lifted a few centimetres, the likely successor to the caesium second; squeezed hard, its electrical resistance rises, so it gauges the pressure of earthquakes and blasts; inside glass fibre it powers the invisible infrared lasers that cut steel — may show in the outfit's details, motifs or small accessories.

Figure: willowy and long-limbed with soft curves — a full bust, rounded hips and a slender waist — keep this exact build from the attached image, neither slimmer nor fuller.

Light: the place's own light, lit and coloured the way this style renders light and skin.

One figure in focus, natural hands with five fingers, no text, logo or watermark.
